name: showreel-39-follow
style: Dark look in the berry colour world, whole frame, calm (E18 kept 15 Nov; E23 dynamic fix try 5; E20 caption ask try 3; BEFORE one clean slide with red signals, AFTER solid with a green lock; owner 15 Nov evening: too wiggly, similar colour grading)

voice.text: Why does your button jump? Follow turns into Following, and the button grows. Everything next to it slides away. The fix: stack both words in one grid cell. The button keeps the longer width. Look closer. The word changes, the button stays. Now your buttons hold still.

caption:
Has a button ever slid away right as you tapped it? yes or never 👇

A Follow button that turns into Following gets wider, and in a row of buttons everything next to it slides over, then slides back when you tap again. The fix is to stack both words in one grid cell: .follow { display: inline-grid; } and .follow span { grid-area: 1 / 1; }, with the word not shown kept as visibility: hidden. A hidden word still takes up its space, so the button is always as wide as "Following" and nothing next to it moves. The same trick works for Play / Pause, Save / Saved and Add / Added.
Send this to whoever builds your profile page, or save it for your next toggle. And answer in the comments: yes or never?

sources.note: MDN grid-area: places an item by its grid lines; grid-area: 1 / 1 puts every label in the first row and column, so they share one cell and the cell is as wide as the widest
MDN visibility: hidden hides the box but it still affects layout (unlike display: none), so the hidden word keeps its width
BCD 8.1.9 (checked 15 Nov 2026), css.properties.grid-area: Chrome 57, Firefox 52, Safari 10.1, Safari iOS 10.3

tip.title: Why does your Follow button jump?
tip.why: A toggle button that changes its word (Follow / Following) changes its width, so everything next to it slides each time it is tapped. Put both words in one grid cell with grid-area: 1 / 1 and hide the one not shown with visibility: hidden: a hidden box still takes its space, so the button always has the width of the longer word. grid-area works in every current browser (Chrome 57+, Firefox 52+, Safari 10.1+; MDN, BCD).
